steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how has the implant been since we last saw you? I usually hear one of three things. Rock solid, something feels a little off, or something is bothering you. Which one is closest?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Rock Solid
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's what a well-placed implant should feel like, so natural you forget which tooth it is. It means the work you invested in is paying off.

(Let them enjoy it. Then ask permission for the questions.)

steps.title: Something Feels a Little Off
steps.content:
I'm glad you mentioned that, {{contact_first_name}}. The gum around an implant needs its own attention, and small changes can start without you noticing. It's not anything you did wrong, and it's the reason we check in. When these things are caught early, they're usually simple to take care of. What got in the way of coming in, life getting busy or feeling like the implant didn't need checkups?

(Let them answer. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Something Is Bothering Them
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}. It's not anything you did wrong. The gum and bone around an implant are living tissue. Things can start there without you noticing. The sooner we look, the simpler it usually is to take care of. What got in the way of coming in, life getting busy or feeling like the implant didn't need checkups?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm updating your file anyway. Can I ask you a few quick questions so it's up to date?

(Wait for the yes. Most people stop thinking about an implant once it feels solid. The questions find what they'd never think to mention.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to what you noticed in a moment. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, around the implant. Any tenderness, swelling, or bleeding when you brush or floss near it?

Do you ever notice food catching around it, or floss snagging nearby?

How does your bite feel on it, chewing on that side like normal?

How about the rest of your teeth, any sensitivity or gum bleeding?

When was your last professional cleaning, here or anywhere?

How do you feel about your smile these days, still smiling in photos?

Finally, any changes in your health or medications since we last saw you?

(Recap what you wrote down, including what they mentioned at the start, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between what you mentioned first and anything else, which one would you most like to take care of?

(If what they mentioned at the start is the only thing on the list, that's the answer. Tap the button and continue.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, around the implant. Any tenderness, swelling, or bleeding when you brush or floss near it?

Do you ever notice food catching around it, or floss snagging nearby?

How does your bite feel on it, chewing on that side like normal?

How about the rest of your teeth, any sensitivity or gum bleeding?

When was your last professional cleaning, here or anywhere?

How do you feel about your smile these days, still smiling in photos?

Finally, any changes in your health or medications since we last saw you?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with meals, talking with people, or smiling in photos?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, a quick implant health check does one thing. {{provider_name}} looks at the implant and the gum and bone holding it. That catches anything small before it becomes something big. If everything is as solid as it feels, we'll tell you that too. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you in for that quick implant health check. Does that sound reasonable?

(Say "does that sound reasonable", not "does that sound good". Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Protect the Investment
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is feeling solid.

(They already told you when their last cleaning was. Use that answer instead of asking again. No judgment either way.)

One thing before I let you go. The implant itself is built to last, but the gum and bone holding it are living tissue. The early warning signs there don't hurt, so you won't feel them until later. A regular cleaning doesn't always include a close look at the implant. A quick check confirms it's as healthy as it feels. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for that quick check so it stays the way it is. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I thought implants were permanent”
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's a fair question, and you're half right. The implant itself is permanent. The gum and bone holding it are living tissue, and they need the same care your natural teeth do. Think of a good roof. The roof lasts for decades, but you still keep the gutters clear. The check is how we keep the permanent part permanent.

Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed I haven’t been in”
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, please don't be. There's no judgment here. Once an implant feels solid, it's natural to stop thinking about it. That's a sign the work was done well. It's the reason we check in. Let's just get your file current and keep it feeling that way.

Would you be open to that?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's the right move.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the other objections. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd find out what the options look like and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at your implant. That's what the visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Is that okay?
